chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ayub ibn Nuh from Ibn Abi Umayr from Muhammad ibn Misar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him: A man gave another man one thousand dirhams as a mudarabah (profit-sharing partnership), and he [the partner] bought his [the investor's] father [as a slave], while he [the partner] did not know that [the money belonged to the investor]. He [the Imam] said: 'It is valued; if it exceeds by one dirham, he is freed, and the man is asked [for the excess].'
And that which indicates what we have previously mentioned regarding the dislike of owning relatives is what he narrated:

key_terms.أَبَاهُ: His father: Referring to the investor's father being bought as a slave by the partner.
key_terms.أُعْتِقَ: He is freed: The slave is emancipated if the value exceeds the capital.
key_terms.اُسْتُسْعِيَ: He is asked: The partner is questioned or asked to pay/return the excess value.
key_terms.كَرَاهِيَةُ مِلْكِ ذَوِي الْأَرْحَامِ: Dislike of owning relatives: A jurisprudential principle regarding the preference against owning one's kin as slaves.
key_terms.مُضَارَبَة: Mudarabah: A profit-sharing partnership in Islamic finance where one party provides capital and the other provides labor.
key_terms.يُقَوَّمُ: It is valued: The legal process of assessing the market value of the purchased item.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a partner using partnership funds to buy a slave for himself without the investor's knowledge?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the ruling on *mudarabah* where a partner inadvertently purchases a slave using the investor's capital. The Imam mandates that the slave be valued; if the market value exceeds the capital by even one dirham, the slave is emancipated, and the partner is held accountable for the surplus, illustrating the principle of *karahiya* (dislike) regarding owning one's relatives.
